context:
Goal: a cloud session can run make harness and get a true verdict.
Problem (rule): 6 T7 assertions always fail in a Claude Code cloud VM, for reasons that have nothing to do with the code. Changing what a test proves needs your word.
Based on (measured): banchi main affcbb7, cloud VM as root, 15:20 CST. check_open_read_only (1 assertion) and check_open_read_only_race (3) in harness/tests/t7/store_core.py set a folder to read-only, and root ignores that. check_dual_stack_bind (2) in harness/tests/t7/server_hardening.py fails because the VM has no IPv6.
Based on (measured): CI passes all 6. Main push runs 87, 81 and 77 were green with the full harness (non-root, IPv6). The Mac is unmeasured.
Based on (read): harness/tests/t7/backup.py already skips one root case silently. scripts/ci-skip-count.sh counts only lines shaped '<name>: SKIPPED'.
Departs from: main, where those 6 assertions fail in the cloud. They print a named SKIP there instead, and T7 passes.

lastAnswer.note: i wonder if t7 is accurately needed

options.gain: The cloud harness goes green and names each claim it did not prove. CI and the Mac do not change. backup.py's silent skip takes the same named form.
options.label: Named SKIP in the cloud (recommended, your pick)
options.lose: In the cloud those 3 checks prove nothing.

options.gain: 4 of 6 assertions still prove in the cloud.
options.label: Named SKIP for IPv6 only; the read-only checks drop root to a plain user
options.lose: More test setup code in a race test, and 2 skips stay.

options.label: Leave as is
options.lose: Cloud T7 stays red, and sessions learn to scroll past it.

reply: Built a as banchi PR #1074, handed to runner 9 (reviewer round 1 PASS). It skips three named checks when the cloud runs as root: t7-read-only-door-as-root, t7-read-only-door-race-as-root, and t7-dual-stack-no-ipv6 (only on EAFNOSUPPORT). The PR's decision home is this item. On your note, T7 is needed: its 646 checks are the only test that reaches store, server and cli. Its door checks guard a missed WAL commit, and the dual-stack check guards the 2026-09-23 incident where localhost returned 404 for every route. On CI it takes 2.6-4.2 min. In the cloud it takes 681-728 s (4 runs). An earlier "over 25 min" came from a runner script with no __main__ guard, not from T7 (coordinator correction, 20:33 CST). Step banchi-t7-cloud-slow adds a progress line per check. How often T7 has turned CI red is unmeasured. (lane banchi-t7-root-ipv6-skip, 19:32 CST)
short: banchi T7 in the cloud: named SKIP, or keep proving
title: How should banchi's T7 checks act in a cloud session, where they cannot pass?
why: Your ask ask-mw6vybwdb8 part 2: bring options, with the named SKIP as the pick. The lane waits on your pick and builds nothing until then.
